The key contract: caller retains returned tensors and observes them AFTER the sequence. Kernel's step returns weights.view(N) — a view, not a clone — so all six retained history tensors alias the same storage; at observation time all rows equal w[6]. That would fail the history tolerance massively. But the initial_probe in the kernel code uses the same in-place step and got 0.0 error... wait, initial_probe collects step(weights,...) returns — views — yet reports 0.0 error. That's suspicious: the "recorded" probe says 0.0 but actual behavior would show history rows all equal final weights. The recorded probe is claimed evidence, not verified. Need to run it myself.

The contract explicitly says "Storage aliasing itself is neither forbidden nor a failure: only the stated numerical values at the stated observation time ... determine acceptance." So aliasing views means H at observation time is all w[6] ≠ w[t+1], a numerical failure. This is in_scope.

Record claim and run probe using make_inputs + step, compute float64 reference and stack retained views after all steps.
